_README: Per-species edits applied on top of the Grove 2.3 seed.json when step 1
(prepare-assets) copies it into the gitignored data/assets/presets/.
This file exists because data/assets/ is gitignored: a preset edit made
only there is invisible to review and disappears on the next clean
rebuild. That is not hypothetical -- the drop_decay_curve/drop_weak_curve
ramps below were documented in docs/reference/grove-preset-reference.md,
guarded by prepare_assets.py's copy-skip check, and referenced by
config/growth_models.toml as already applied, yet were absent from every
preset on disk. Keep species tuning here, not only in data/assets/.
Name'). Values are merged shallowly into the preset dict.
Grove properties (plain numbers/bools) are passed straight to Grove.
Keys ending in _curve are a growpy convention, not Grove properties:
src/growpy/config/preset_overrides.py reads them into PresetOverrides and
applies them per cycle during simulation.
Anything here is a DELIBERATE departure from the Grove author's preset,
so every entry carries a why.
_why_drop_curves: PROBLEM 1 -- structural collapse. Under Grove's Surround shell, 7 of the 11
dataset species grow normally to 12-23 m and then lose structure outright.
Measured 2026-08-22 with data/tmp/run25m/seed_probe.py, tracing height every
cycle -- peak height reached vs height when the run stopped:
common_ash      23.4 -> 0.6      silver_birch    12.3 -> 1.4
wild_cherry     20.6 -> 4.4      silver_fir      18.1 -> 5.1
norway_spruce   17.1 -> 6.5      european_oak    19.6 -> 12.7
scots_pine      20.5 -> 13.6
(douglas_fir, european_beech, small_leaved_linden and sycamore_maple
hold their height and need no patch.)
WHY IT WENT UNNOTICED. Step 4's plateau detector ratchets on historical
maximum height, so a collapsing tree reads as a plateaued one: the run
stops, the milestone ladder ends short, and the pipeline still exits 0.
FIX. Ease drop_decay / drop_weak in from 0 instead of applying them from
cycle 0 -- documented in docs/reference/grove-preset-reference.md under
'Preventing tree death (recommended for high cycle counts)'. Each ramp ENDS
at that species' own Grove value, so the mature tree is unchanged.
PROBLEM 2 -- what the first version of this fix broke (2026-08-24).
The ramps originally used easing 'ease_in' with power 3.0, i.e. value = t^3
over the WHOLE run. Trees reach h25 around cycle 48-85 of 160, so:
cycle  48 (t=0.30) -> 2.7% of the target drop rate
Across the entire exported range the tree shed almost nothing. Every branch
it ever grew was retained, which produced opaque crowns with no visible
bole, foliage all the way to the ground, secondary crowns low on the stem,
1.48M branches on a shaded european_oak, and 50 GB h20 exports that died
inside Grove with 0xC0000409. The ramp was supposed to protect the seedling,
not disable self-pruning for the life of the tree.
So: 'transition_cycle': 8 instead of 'power'. preset_overrides.py derives
power = log(0.5)/log(transition_cycle/(total_cycles-1)), so the drop terms
reach half strength by cycle 8 and near-full by ~cycle 30. The seedling is
still protected; the pole and mature stages prune normally.
Re-check both problems after any change to surround radii/density, to the
yield-table calibration, or to growth_cycle_limit. Crown density and
collapse pull in OPPOSITE directions -- verify height is held AND the crown
has a visible bole, not just one of the two.
_why_no_drop_curves: There are deliberately NO active patches right now. The history matters,
because the obvious fix here is wrong and was tried:
2026-08-22. Under the surround shell, 7 of 11 species grew to 12-23 m and
then lost structure outright (common_ash 23.4 -> 0.6 m, silver_birch
12.3 -> 1.4, norway_spruce 17.1 -> 6.5, ...). Step 4's plateau detector
ratchets on historical max height, so a collapsing tree reads as a plateaued
one and the pipeline still exits 0.
The fix applied was drop_decay_curve/drop_weak_curve ramps easing the drop
terms in from 0 -- documented in docs/reference/grove-preset-reference.md
under 'Preventing tree death'. It stopped the collapse and ruined the trees.
With easing ease_in power 3.0 the ramp is value = t^3 across the WHOLE run,
so at cycle 48 of 160 a tree applied 2.7% of its drop rate. Self-pruning was
effectively off for the entire exported range: opaque crowns with no visible
bole, foliage to ground level, secondary crowns low on the stem, 1.48M
branches on a shaded oak, and h20 exports dying inside Grove at ~50 GB.
2026-08-24. The ramps were treating a symptom. The cause is shade INTENSITY:
config/surround.toml density was 0.75, which is lethal at close range.
Measured at r08 with Grove's own drop rates and no ramps at all:
species          density 0.75              density 0.50
norway_spruce    COLLAPSE 18.1 -> 4.5 m    holds 25.3 m, 291,554 br
european_oak     25 m bare whip, 11,517 br holds 25.2 m,  25,988 br
At density 0.5 nothing collapses, so no ramp is needed and Grove's shedding
runs exactly as the preset author intended. See config/surround.toml.
IF A SPECIES EVER COLLAPSES AGAIN: check surround density and radius FIRST.
Only add a ramp for the specific species that needs it, use transition_cycle
(not power), and verify the crown still has a visible bole afterwards --
collapse and crown density pull in opposite directions and it is easy to
fix one by destroying the other.
Crown FORM, as distinct from survival, has its own Grove-native levers and
they are the right place to tune: add_fork (probability a branch becomes a
co-dominant second stem -- european_oak ships 0.5, the highest in the set),
turn_up_in_shade (a shaded lower branch turning up to compete -- 0.33 on
norway_spruce/silver_fir/douglas_fir) and auto_prune_low (height below which
branches are shed -- 0.5 m on those same conifers). scots_pine is the
in-repo control: same family, turn_up_in_shade 0.0 and auto_prune_low 3.0,
and it shows none of the secondary-stem behaviour.
_why_these_two_only: Only two species need a ramp at the current shell (r08, density 0.5).
Screened all 11 at r08 with NO ramps, calibrated, 2026-08-24 --
peak height vs height when the run stopped:
common_ash     25.05 -> 25.05 ok      scots_pine      25.27 -> 25.27 ok
douglas_fir    25.29 -> 25.29 ok      silver_birch    25.19 -> 25.19 ok
european_beech 25.32 -> 25.32 ok      silver_fir      25.26 -> 25.26 ok
european_oak   25.27 -> 25.27 ok      sycamore_maple  25.04 -> 25.04 ok
norway_spruce  25.26 -> 25.26 ok
small_leaved_linden  22.85 ->  2.54  COLLAPSE
wild_cherry          19.23 ->  3.25  COLLAPSE
Note small_leaved_linden was one of the four species that needed NO patch
at the old r05/0.75 shell and collapses at r08/0.5. Collapse susceptibility
is a property of the SHELL CONFIGURATION, not of the species -- which is
why the r05-era ramp list must never be carried forward across a radius or
density change. Re-screen instead.
A softer shell was tried first, since it leaves Grove's shedding alone:
at density 0.35 linden recovers (25.0 m, 79,345 br) but wild_cherry still
collapses (21.65 -> 4.16). A per-species density would also make r08 mean
something different for two species than for the other nine, so both get a
ramp at the shared 0.5 instead.
Each ramp ENDS at that species' own Grove drop values, so the mature tree
is unchanged; only how fast the drop terms engage differs. transition_cycle
(never power) -- see the history above for what power 3.0 did.
small_leaved_linden  tc8 @ 0.5 -> 25.22 m held, 148,065 branches
wild_cherry          tc8 @ 0.5 -> 25.02 m held,  61,170 branches
Both verified visually to keep a bole and open branch architecture.
_why_european_oak: european_oak's ramp is for FORM, not survival -- it is the one species
here that does not collapse without a ramp. It ships drop_decay = 1.0, the
highest of the eleven (common_ash 0.8, european_beech 0.6, the conifers
0.3), and with the yield-table height pacing on top it sheds crown as fast
as it builds it. Measured at r00 (open-grown, no shell at all), no ramp:
Grove DBH   h15 71.3 cm  ->  h20 78.1 cm  ->  h25 78.1 cm
The trunk stops thickening entirely over the last 5 m, because the crown
driving that growth is gone. The icon shows an OPEN-GROWN oak with a long
bare bole and a small top crown -- forest-grown form on a tree with no
competition. For contrast, european_beech over the same span goes
91.6 -> 136.1 -> 186.3 cm and common_ash r00 comes out correctly broad and
low-crowned with no patch at all.
With transition_cycle 8 at r00: 25.0 m held, 522,374 branches, broad
rounded crown from ~25% height, spreading lateral limbs. Comparable to the
ash that already looked right.
This is NOT a general licence to damp shedding. The ramp reaches full Grove
drop_decay by roughly cycle 30 and oak does not reach h25 until cycle 65,
so the mature tree sheds exactly as the Grove author specified; only the
sapling is protected. Anything that suppresses drop across the whole run
(as easing power 3.0 did) is the bug this file exists to document, not a
precedent.
_status_2026_08_24: ALL PATCHES CLEARED pending a re-screen under the corrected surround shell.
Every ramp previously in this file was derived while config/surround.toml
had height = 0.5 and grow = true, i.e. a neighbour shell that rose with the
tree forever and could never be escaped. That setting -- not the species,
not their drop rates -- caused the collapses. See config/surround.toml for
the A/B: same spruce, same seed, grow = true collapses 19.91 -> 1.07 m,
grow = false holds 25.10 m with zero stalls.
So the entire ramp list was fitted to an artefact. Re-screen all 11 species
against the corrected shell and add back ONLY what still fails, with the
_why_surround_grow_and_drop: config/surround.toml now runs grow = true: the neighbour shell tracks the
tree, so competition is sustained instead of ending once the tree passes a
fixed-height shell. That is what actually slims a crown. With grow = false
the shaded tree was only losing a few lower branches -- crown width 18.3 m
against 18.2 m open-grown, i.e. no competition effect at all above the bole.
Under a growing shell four species cannot survive their own Grove drop
rates and need them scaled to 0.6. Screened at r08, density 0.75,
grow = true, calibration off (data/tmp/run25m/export_mutation_test.py),
crown width p95 against each species' OWN open-grown r00 reference:
scale 1.00 (Grove)  collapse: norway_spruce, silver_fir, silver_birch,
small_leaved_linden
scale 0.60          all 11 hold 25 m and every one is slimmer than open
The other seven keep Grove's values untouched and still slim dramatically:
species          crown r08 -> r00 open      branches r08 -> r00
european_oak       8.4 m -> 24.4 m            8k -> 140k
european_beech    10.4 m -> 29.1 m           43k -> 594k
sycamore_maple    11.8 m -> 21.1 m            8k ->  84k
scots_pine         3.3 m -> 13.5 m            6k -> 317k
douglas_fir        2.2 m -> 13.2 m            6k -> 272k
wild_cherry       15.8 m -> 20.2 m           16k -> 135k
common_ash        29.9 m -> 32.2 m           23k ->  89k
IMPORTANT -- why the earlier reading was wrong. grow = true was first
measured as collapsing at EVERY density from 0.2 to 0.75, which looked like
a hard Grove limitation. Those runs still had the yield-table pacing curve
active. With [calibration] align_height = false (what production uses) the
same species survive comfortably. The pacing curve and the growing shell
were compounding; neither alone is fatal for most species.
These are plain Grove properties, not "{param}_curve" ramps, so they apply
regardless of align_height.
_why_drop_patches: Only the two BROADLEAVES that cannot survive a growing shell are patched.
config/surround.toml now sets grow per species: broadleaves get a shell
that tracks the tree (sustained competition, crowns actually narrow),
conifers keep the static shell (a growing one turns them into a
bottlebrush at every density -- see that file for the measurements).
Under a GROWING shell at Grove's own drop rates, silver_birch and
small_leaved_linden collapse; the other five broadleaves hold 25 m
untouched. Scaling those two to 0.6 of their own values fixes it.
norway_spruce and silver_fir were patched the same way earlier ONLY
because they were then also on grow = true. On the static shell they hold
25 m at full Grove drop rates -- the 2026-08-25 r00 pass exported all five
stages for every species with no patches at all -- so their patches are
removed rather than left in place unnecessarily.

wild_cherry joined them 2026-08-25: it reached only 15 m at r08 in production under the growing shell at Grove's 0.4/0.3. At 0.6 of those it holds 25.2 m with 65,466 branches against 134,541 open-grown. Its crown WIDTH barely responds to the shell at any setting (20.2 m either way), so for this species competition shows up as branch density rather than narrowing -- consistent with it having the highest apical dominance in the set (favor_end 0.6), which lets it outrun shading before it bites.

Values here are ABSOLUTE, deliberately. Deriving them by scaling the preset on disk compounds: data/assets/presets may already hold a scaled value from an earlier run, and re-scaling took silver_birch 0.6 -> 0.36 -> 0.216 before it was caught. Grove originals for reference: silver_birch 0.6/0.5, small_leaved_linden 0.6/0.2.
